description: Canonical role/model routing matrix for ekucher/BRAVO-Toolkit. Normative agent-orchestration rules live in BRAVO_AGENT_POLICY.md; this file is the machine-readable source of truth for role-to-model assignment, risk-level gates and fallback limits. Operator documentation: docs/ai/MODEL_ROUTING_POLICY.md.

worker.writeDenyNote: No writeAllow: an implementer writes code, so its real boundary is the task SCOPE, which the hook cannot see at write time. These denies are the subset that holds regardless of any brief.

tester.purpose: test authoring inside assigned SCOPE; never production code

documentation.purpose: audits code-vs-documentation drift always; writes documentation only under an explicit SCOPE

reviewer.purpose: fresh Claude internal pre-review, or temporary QA fallback under BRAVO_AGENT_POLICY.md section 8.2

architect.purpose: design and architectural risk analysis; never closes the formal Codex architecture gate

security-reviewer.purpose: internal security pre-review; never closes the formal Codex security gate

HIGH.examples: cross-module contracts, configuration, installer, significant behavior change

CRITICAL.examples: backup/restore, security, integrity, Scheduler/SYSTEM, authentication, data-loss risk

fallback.notes: A forbidden reason is a defect to diagnose, not a fallback trigger (BRAVO_AGENT_POLICY.md section 8.2). When Codex and the Claude fallback reviewer are both unavailable, the gate is reported NOT RUN / blocked; there is no second-level fallback to a weaker model.

documentationTriggers.note: Any change with one of these externally observable effects requires the documentation role regardless of risk level.
effects: new or changed CLI parameter or switch
changed Scheduled Task definition or service behavior
changed persisted state format or path
changed notification or log contract relied on operationally

enforcement.delegationToolNote: The delegation tool is named Agent in Claude Code 2.1.x; Task is kept for versions that named it so. Both must stay gated: a live run on 2026-10-12 showed the hook receives tool_name=Agent, and while only Task was listed every delegation check was skipped as 'not subject to routing policy'.

writeGate.note: The write boundary is enforced on the actual write, keyed on the acting agent from the PreToolUse agent_type field, not only on the SCOPE text of a delegation brief.
writeGate.mainSessionNote: agent_type is absent in the main session; gating it would block the owner's own work. The system constrains delegated executors, not the owner of the process.
writeGate.bashNote: Bash is deliberately NOT gated: inspecting an arbitrary command for what it would write is a heuristic with guaranteed bypasses. The answer for Bash is to withhold the tool from write-bounded roles, which is why the documentation role has no Bash.

enforcement.unmanagedAgentsNote: Agents absent from roles (Explore, general-purpose, plugin agents) are logged, never blocked.
enforcement.failOpenNote: If the hook itself fails, gate-critical roles are blocked and every other call is allowed with a loud [HOOK-ERROR] log entry.
